predictions.statement: The US Federal Trade Commission will issue at least one formal information demand or compel testimony from an organisation covered by its industry-wide AI-agent inquiry by 2026-10-30.
predictions.successCondition: A regulator, covered organisation or reliable report confirms that the FTC issued a formal demand for information or compelled testimony in the inquiry on or before 2026-10-30.
predictions.failureCondition: Reliable verification covering the full window establishes that no such formal demand or compelled testimony occurred by the end of 2026-10-30.

sources.label: Reuters report on the FTC inquiry

outlookSnapshot.assessment: Artificial-intelligence development is likely to remain dominated by rapid infrastructure expansion and widening deployment of autonomous agents, accompanied by closer regulatory and security scrutiny. The FTC's industry-wide inquiry shows that US oversight is moving beyond voluntary commitments, while Google's controlled Gemini 4 rollout and Micron's supply constraints indicate that safety evaluation and infrastructure capacity will shape near-term competition.
likelyDevelopments: Major AI developers will publish or clarify how they intend to implement the US accord's internal controls and external reviews.
Security providers and large technology companies will expand runtime controls and automated cyber defences for autonomous agents.
Investment in chips, data centres and physical-AI capabilities will continue, while investors focus more closely on the cost and financing of frontier-model development.
Governments and standards bodies will continue translating broad AI-safety principles into more specific auditing and assurance practices.

upcomingEvents.description: Ireland is scheduled to host the International AI Summit on 14 October as the official launch of European AI Innovation Month.

Large new infrastructure commitments, cancellations or financing problems

predictions.statement: The United States or Iran will publicly confirm another substantive mediator-facilitated exchange or negotiation concerning Gulf de-escalation by 2026-10-26.
predictions.successCondition: An official statement or reliable report confirms that US and Iranian representatives exchanged substantive proposals or held indirect or direct talks through a mediator about Gulf de-escalation on or before 2026-10-26.
predictions.failureCondition: Reliable verification covering the full window establishes that no further substantive mediator-facilitated exchange or negotiation was publicly confirmed by the end of 2026-10-26.

sources.label: US response to Iran's seven-day proposal
Economic pressure from disrupted fuel supplies

outlookSnapshot.assessment: Iran is likely to continue indirect talks through regional mediators while resisting US demands for nuclear concessions. No agreement followed Tehran's receipt of the US response, and the widening diesel shortage is increasing pressure on Washington and European governments to secure maritime de-escalation, but negotiations still lack an agreed sequence of concessions.
likelyDevelopments: Tehran will continue to link freer passage through the Strait of Hormuz to relief from the US naval blockade and other economic pressure.
Iran will resist nuclear concessions in the near-term shipping negotiations, leaving the nuclear dispute on a separate and slower track.
The United States will press China and regional partners to use their economic and diplomatic leverage over Tehran.

Iran is likely to revise or re-present phased proposals through mediators while maintaining military readiness, but an immediate durable agreement is unlikely after Washington rejected the current offer.

upcomingEvents.description: The European Council is scheduled to meet on 15–16 October, providing a potential coordination point for European policy on Middle East security and shipping disruption.

predictions.statement: A Russian attack will again damage transport or energy infrastructure in Kyiv and cause an officially confirmed service disruption by 2026-10-26.
predictions.successCondition: Ukrainian authorities or reliable reporting confirms that a Russian attack after 2026-10-03 damaged transport or energy infrastructure in Kyiv and disrupted traffic, electricity, heating or another public service on or before 2026-10-26.
predictions.failureCondition: Reliable verification covering the full window establishes that no such Russian attack caused an officially confirmed service disruption in Kyiv by the end of 2026-10-26.

sources.label: Russian strike on Kyiv Northern Bridge

outlookSnapshot.assessment: Russia is likely to sustain intensive attacks on Ukraine's urban, transport and energy infrastructure through the approaching winter while maintaining coercive pressure on Europe. Repeated strikes on Kyiv's Dnipro bridges demonstrate a more systematic effort to disrupt movement inside the capital, reinforcing the prospect of escalation despite proposals for limited truces.
likelyDevelopments: Russian drone and missile operations against Ukraine will continue, with jet-powered drones placing additional pressure on Ukrainian air defences.
European governments will strengthen their response to Russian sabotage, cyber activity and military movements around NATO airspace.

Diplomatic activity will probably continue through selective bilateral contacts and discussions about maritime security or energy infrastructure, but a comprehensive settlement remains unlikely during the forecast period.
The Kremlin will use the parliamentary-election result to reinforce the appearance of domestic support and institutional stability.

upcomingEvents.description: EU restrictive measures addressing Russian hybrid activity are currently scheduled to expire, creating a decision point over renewal or replacement.
The European Council is scheduled to meet on 15–16 October and has said it will return to Ukraine and European defence readiness in October.

changeSignals: Russian acceptance of talks on a Black Sea or energy-infrastructure truce
A substantial reduction or increase in long-range attacks on Ukrainian cities
New EU sanctions or military-support commitments
Confirmed escalation involving Russian and NATO aircraft or infrastructure
Evidence that post-election domestic pressure is affecting Kremlin policy

predictions.successCondition: A maritime authority, government or reliable report confirms that a commercial tanker was attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz after 2026-10-06 and on or before 2026-10-26.
predictions.failureCondition: Reliable verification covering the full window establishes that no commercial tanker was attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz by the end of 2026-10-26.

sources.label: Middle East oil exports recover while tanker attacks rise
Iran reiterates seven conditions for reopening Hormuz

outlookSnapshot.assessment: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is likely to remain selective and hazardous even as Gulf oil exports recover through adapted routes and guarded transits. Iran continues to condition a formal reopening on seven US steps, while rising tanker attacks, exceptional freight costs and weak refined-fuel flows show that higher export volumes have not restored normal maritime operations.
likelyDevelopments: Negotiators and mediators will probably explore revised staged steps that exchange greater freedom of navigation for relief from US pressure on Iranian ports.
Commercial shipping and energy markets will remain sensitive to tanker attacks, insurance costs and conflicting statements from Washington and Tehran.
Regional states will seek additional security coordination while avoiding actions that could expand the conflict.
Any initial accord is more likely to be narrow and operational than a comprehensive political settlement.

upcomingEvents.description: The European Council meets on 15–16 October, when the economic and security consequences of disrupted Gulf shipping may require further coordination.

US relief from the naval blockade or sanctions affecting Iranian ports

Attacks on tankers, ports or naval forces
Changes in insurance costs, rerouting, guarded transits or energy-market disruption
